desc:
The string s contains only the characters '(', ')' and '*'. Each '*' is a joker that you may independently treat as '(', as ')', or as an empty string (nothing at all).

Return true if the jokers can be resolved so that the resulting string is well-formed: every '(' is closed by a later ')', every ')' closes an earlier '(', and nothing is left open.

For example "(*)" and "(*))" are valid, while ")*(" is not.
hints: Trying all 3k ways to resolve k stars is far too slow. Instead of one running balance, think about the set of balances that are still possible after each character.
That set is always an interval of consecutive integers (clipped at 0). You only need its smallest and largest possible balance.
Keep lo and hi. For '(' add 1 to both, for ')' subtract 1 from both, for '*' do lo -= 1, hi += 1. If hi < 0 return false; clamp lo at 0. At the end the string is valid exactly when lo == 0.
editorial: Let lo be the smallest and hi the largest number of unclosed brackets you could have after reading a prefix, over all ways to resolve its stars (never letting the balance drop below 0 on the way). A '(' raises both, a ')' lowers both, and a '*' can lower the minimum by one (as ')') and raise the maximum by one (as '('); it can also do nothing, which keeps every value in between reachable.

If hi becomes negative, even the most generous reading has a stray ')', so the answer is false. A negative lo is simply clamped to 0, because a reading that would go below 0 is not allowed and the in-between values stay reachable. At the end, the string can be balanced if 0 is inside the interval, which, after clamping, means lo == 0. This is O(n) time and O(1) space. A two-stack solution (indices of unmatched ( and of *, matched greedily at the end) reaches the same answer.
